posts.author: matsnil
posts.text: · HFI Research i morges: At the end of September, I wrote that the market was incorrectly assuming that the Oman Lane flows would continue. Financial writers were so eager to proclaim that 1) Iran lost control and 2) oil flows are going back to normal. That turned out to be a very bad call. The reality right now is that the Oman Lane transit flows continue. As of the latest figures I’ve seen, implied Strait of Hormuz flow is somewhere between 8 and 9 million b/d, down from 13-14 million b/d. The forward-looking implied flow (over the next 10 days) is expected to fall to 6-7 million b/d. For the moment, oil traders continue to see the latest attacks as transitory. We are not seeing any material panic in the physical market just yet. The surge in crude volumes out of the Strait of Hormuz in mid-September is enough to calm things down a bit just as global refineries enter maintenance this time of the year, but I suspect elevated tanker rates are masking some of the inherent panic to come. Ganske mange VLCC ser ut til å ha endret kurs og ikke gått inn i sundet etter Irans eskalering
